comparison: Perfect alignment on transcriptomic findings (C3, C33, C39-C48, C100-C101). Both evaluations find the differential expression analysis and GSEA results well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes statistical methods and cross-validation with human IBD datasets, while peer reviewers acknowledge the findings as 'compelling' though note they are 'observational and correlative.'

Perfect alignment on ModQTL mapping methodology (C35, C80-C82). Both evaluations confirm the QTL analysis on chromosome 16 and the candidate gene prioritization approach. OpenEval validates the statistical methods (permutation testing, LOCO kinship correction), while peer reviewers confirm the identification of 27 prioritized genes from 552 protein-coding genes.

Strong alignment on strain classification (C49-C50, C52-C54, C107). Both evaluations support the identification of susceptible and resistant BXD strains. Peer review R2 additionally covers cytokine findings (C55-C56, C102) not included in OpenEval R3, confirming IL-10 and IL-15 differences between strain groups.

Partial overlap on cytokine measurements (C55-C56, C102). OpenEval R4 focuses specifically on plasma cytokine data with statistical validation, while peer review R2 includes this as part of broader strain classification findings. Both confirm increased IL-10 and IL-15 in resistant strains.

Strong alignment on WGCNA co-expression analysis (C34, C61-C67). Both evaluations confirm the identification of gene modules correlating with mouse UC and human IBD datasets. OpenEval emphasizes statistical thresholds and overlap with CD modules, while peer reviewers describe the analyses as 'compelling.' Peer review R3 includes C105 not in OpenEval R5.

Strong alignment on transcription factor analysis (C4, C68-C70, C74-C77, C106). Both evaluations confirm TF motif enrichment and cell-type analyses were conducted. OpenEval finds the methods appropriate with clear statistical thresholds, while peer reviewers acknowledge the work but emphasize it remains 'observational and correlative' without experimental validation of regulatory predictions.

Substantial overlap on candidate gene identification (C5, C83-C90, C93-C94). Both evaluations address the prioritization of EPHA6 and MUC4 through integration of mouse ModQTL, literature mining, and human GWAS data. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes GWAS p-values don't reach genome-wide significance. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing results are 'observational and correlative' requiring future experimental validation.

Significant overlap on translational inferences and causal claims (C6, C95-C99, C108). Both evaluations express uncertainty about causal interpretations. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to nominal MR significance without multiple testing correction and speculative conclusions about HFD-induced inflammation as UC prelude. Peer reviewers similarly note lack of 'mechanistic or causation-focused investigations,' describing these as hypotheses for future investigation.

OpenEval R1 evaluates background and literature citations (C1-C2, C7-C32) establishing scientific context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on novel findings rather than background claims.
OpenEval R10 evaluates established fact about DSS-induced colitis models (C51). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as this is standard background knowledge.

OpenEval R11 evaluates general genetics principle motivating ModQTL approach (C104). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers did not separately assess methodological rationale citations.
